proposals.before: The court summoned him as Major to the Minister of State, Chief Clerk, and Palace Assistant Censor, then promoted him to Director of the Department of State Affairs and enfeoffed him as Marquis of An'guo Village.
proposals.after: The court summoned him as Major to the Minister of State, Chief Clerk, and Palace Assistant Censor, then promoted him to Shangshu and enfeoffed him as Marquis of An'guo Village.
proposals.reason: Chinese 遷尚書 is promotion to Shangshu, not 尚書令 (Director of the Department of State Affairs), the office already associated with his father.

proposals.before: Chen Yu, style Xianchu, rose through supernumerary gentleman and Luoyang magistrate to palace attendant, then led the left colonel's corps, ran the Ministry of Agriculture, and returned to the palace corps.
proposals.after: Yu, courtesy name Xianchu, was appointed Cavalier Gentleman-in-Attendance and Magistrate of Luoyang, promoted to Gentleman of the Yellow Gate, then served successively as colonel of the Left Army, Minister of Agriculture, and Palace Attendant.
proposals.reason: 厲/歷將校左軍 is successive service, not 'led the left colonel's corps'; 黃門侍郎 is not the same office as 侍中 (palace attendant), which appears only at the end of the sequence.

proposals.before: Shuang took him on staff; Xiu succeeded to the Qingyang village fief and entered the palace corps.
proposals.after: Shuang therefore summoned him as an aide; Xiu inherited his father's Qingyang village marquisate and was promoted to Gentleman of the Yellow Gate.
proposals.reason: 黃門侍郎 is Gentleman of the Yellow Gate, not a generic palace-corps/Palace Attendant (侍中) appointment.

proposals.before: Shuang therefore summoned him as an aide; Xiu inherited his father's Qingyang village marquisate and was promoted to Palace Attendant.
proposals.after: Shuang therefore summoned him as an aide; Xiu inherited his father's Qingyang village marquisate and was promoted to Gentleman of the Yellow Gate.
proposals.reason: Same office mistranslation of 黃門侍郎 as Palace Attendant.

proposals.before: He was summoned to serve as Major to the Minister of State, Chief Clerk, and Palace Assistant Censor, then promoted to Director of the Department of State Affairs and enfeoffed as Marquis of the An'guo village.
proposals.after: He was summoned to serve as Major to the Minister of State, Chief Clerk, and Palace Assistant Censor, then promoted to Shangshu and enfeoffed as Marquis of the An'guo village.
proposals.reason: Chinese 遷尚書 names the Shangshu post, not 尚書令 (Director of the Department of State Affairs).

proposals.before: When the emperor campaigned against Zhuge Dan, Xiu accompanied Minister of the Left Chen Tai and Palace Attendant Zhong Hui with the mobile headquarters staff and took part in strategic planning.
proposals.after: When the emperor campaigned against Zhuge Dan, Xiu accompanied Vice Director of the Imperial Secretariat Chen Tai and Gentleman of the Yellow Gate Zhong Hui with the mobile headquarters staff and took part in strategic planning.
proposals.reason: 尚書僕射 is vice director of the secretariat, not Minister of the Left, and 黃門侍郎 is Gentleman of the Yellow Gate, not Palace Attendant.

proposals.before: When Dan was suppressed, Xiu was transferred to Director of the Department of State Affairs, advanced to Marquis of the Luyang district, with an additional thousand households.
proposals.after: When Dan was suppressed, Xiu was transferred to be a Shangshu, advanced to Marquis of the Luyang district, with an additional thousand households.
proposals.reason: 轉尚書 is transfer to a Shangshu post, not 尚書令, an office Xiu only receives later.

proposals.before: When the Duke of Changdao was enthroned, Xiu shared in the preliminary council that fixed the succession; he was advanced to county marquis with seven hundred more households and promoted to Minister of the Left.
proposals.after: When the Duke of Changdao was enthroned, Xiu shared in the preliminary council that fixed the succession; he was advanced to county marquis with seven hundred more households and promoted to Vice Director of the Imperial Secretariat.
proposals.reason: 遷尚書僕射 is promotion to vice director of the secretariat, not specifically Minister of the Left.

proposals.before: After Emperor Wu had taken the position of king, he appointed Pei Xiu Secretariat Director and Right Guanglu Grandee. Together with Censor-in-chief Wang Shen and General Who Guards Jia Chong, Pei Xiu opened an office, and he was additionally made Palace Attendant.
proposals.after: After Emperor Wu had taken the position of king, he appointed Pei Xiu Secretariat Director and Right Guanglu Grandee. Together with Censor-in-chief Wang Shen and General Who Guards Jia Chong, Pei Xiu opened an office, and he was additionally made Given Attendance within the Palace.
proposals.reason: 給事中 is not Palace Attendant; it is the concurrent inner-court post of given attendance.

proposals.before: After Emperor Wu had taken the position of king, he appointed Pei Xiu Secretariat Director and Right Guanglu Grandee. Together with Censor-in-chief Wang Shen and General Who Guards Jia Chong, Pei Xiu opened an office, and he was additionally made Palace Attendant.
proposals.after: After Emperor Wu had taken the position of king, he appointed Pei Xiu Secretariat Director and Right Guanglu Grandee. Together with Censor-in-chief Wang Shen and General Who Guards Jia Chong, Pei Xiu opened an office, and he was additionally made Given Attendance within the Palace.
proposals.reason: The literal column repeats the same mistranslation of 給事中 as Palace Attendant.

proposals.before: The dull illegitimate Jing received a minor Gaoyang village marquisate while the legitimate junior uncle Yi took the primary succession.
proposals.after: Jun's dull-witted son by a concubine, Jing, was separately enfeoffed as Marquis of the Gaoyang village, and Jun's younger brother Yi succeeded to the main line.
proposals.reason: The idiomatic rendering invents 'legitimate junior uncle' and omits Jun as the stated father and elder brother.

proposals.before: As Yang Jun fell, Liu Yu—Jun's colonel of the left—blocked the gate and demanded Sima Liang's whereabouts.
proposals.after: When Yang Jun was about to be executed, Jun's partisan General of the Left Army Liu Yu deployed troops at the gate; he met Yi and asked where the Grand Tutor was.
proposals.reason: Idiomatic English omits 遇頠 and replaces the source title 太傅 with the unstated personal name Sima Liang.

proposals.before: Yi lied that he had seen the grand tutor leave west through the western portal in a plain cart."
proposals.after: Yi lied that he had seen the grand tutor leave west through the Western Lateral Gate in a plain cart.
proposals.reason: Trailing stray quotation mark corrupts the sentence; 西掖門 is the Western Lateral Gate.

proposals.before: At the time, Chen Zhun's son Kuang and Han Wei's son Song were both serving in the Eastern Palace. Wei remonstrated, saying, "The establishment of the Eastern Palace is to store up the imperial standard.
proposals.after: At the time, Chen Zhun's son Kuang and Han Wei's son Song were both serving in the Eastern Palace. Wei remonstrated, saying, "The Eastern Palace is established to uphold the heir as the imperial pole.
proposals.reason: 儲皇極 concerns the heir (儲) as the imperial pole, not storing a standard.

proposals.before: Yi deeply worried that the age's unrestrained customs did not honor Confucian teaching. He Yan and Ruan Ji enjoyed lofty reputations, talking idle emptiness and ignoring ritual law, drawing salary and indulging favor while holding office yet doing nothing.
proposals.after: Pei Wei deeply worried that the age's unrestrained customs did not honor Confucian teaching. He Yan and Ruan Ji enjoyed lofty reputations, talking idle emptiness and ignoring ritual law, drawing salary and indulging favor while holding office yet doing nothing.
proposals.reason: The subject 頠 is the same Pei Wei named later in this treatise; rendering him as Yi here and Pei Wei afterward splits one person across two English names.

proposals.before: Yi deeply worried that the customs of the age were unrestrained and did not honor Confucian teaching; He Yan and Ruan Ji enjoyed lofty reputations in the world, talking idle emptiness at the mouth and not observing ritual law—drawing salary and indulging favor while holding office yet doing nothing.
proposals.after: Pei Wei deeply worried that the customs of the age were unrestrained and did not honor Confucian teaching; He Yan and Ruan Ji enjoyed lofty reputations in the world, talking idle emptiness at the mouth and not observing ritual law—drawing salary and indulging favor while holding office yet doing nothing.
proposals.reason: Literal English likewise uses Yi for 頠, which is Pei Wei; the later owned units already translate the same name as Pei Wei.

proposals.before: Princes Sima Yong of Liang and Sima Yue of Donghai declared that Yi's father Xiu had served the dynasty and received offerings in the Grand Temple—his line must not be extinguished—so the boys lived on, banished to Daifang.
proposals.after: Princes Sima Rong of Liang and Sima Yue of Donghai declared that Yi's father Xiu had served the dynasty and received offerings in the Grand Temple—his line must not be extinguished—so the boys lived on, banished to Daifang.
proposals.reason: Chinese 梁王肜 is Sima Rong, not Sima Yong; the idiomatic line already has Rong.

proposals.before: Gai had been posthumously adopted to uncle Kai; he was supernumerary attendant until both brothers fell to Chen Wu's Qi Huo band.
proposals.after: Gai had been adopted out to his father's cousin Kai; he was supernumerary attendant until both brothers fell to Chen Wu's Qi Huo band.
proposals.reason: 出後 marks adoption as heir during life, not a posthumous adoption.

proposals.before: His father Wei had been Governor of Jizhou under Wei.
proposals.after: His father Hui had been Governor of Jizhou under Wei.
proposals.reason: 父徽 is Hui; the literal line confuses the person with the polity 魏.

proposals.before: He built a villa; cousin Wang Yan coveted it, so Kai gave him the house outright.
proposals.after: He built a villa; his elder cousin Yan coveted it, so Kai gave him the house outright.
proposals.reason: Chinese 從兄衍 does not name Wang Yan; later Kai tells Wang Yan they never knew each other.

proposals.before: Sudden killings terrified Luoyang.
proposals.after: Sudden killings terrified everyone.
proposals.reason: Chinese 眾人為之震恐 is the assembled people, not the place-name Luoyang.

proposals.before: At first the Pei and Wang houses flourished side by side in the Wei-Jin age; contemporaries likened eight Peis to eight Wangs: Wei to Wang Xiang, Kai to Wang Yan, Kang to Wang Sui, Chuo to Wang Cheng, Zan to Wang Dun, Xia to Wang Dao, Yi to Wang Rong, and Miao to Wang Xuanyun.
proposals.after: At first the Pei and Wang houses flourished side by side in the Wei-Jin age; contemporaries likened eight Peis to eight Wangs: Hui to Wang Xiang, Kai to Wang Yan, Kang to Wang Sui, Chuo to Wang Cheng, Zan to Wang Dun, Xia to Wang Dao, Yi to Wang Rong, and Miao to Wang Xuan.
proposals.reason: 徽 is Hui, not Wei; 王玄雲 uses 雲 as a sentence particle, not a two-character name Xuanyun.

proposals.before: He sobered into scholarship and stayed home.
proposals.after: By adulthood he had reformed to solemn dignity and cultivated Confucian learning; for several years his feet did not cross the threshold.
proposals.reason: The idiomatic line drops 弱冠, 折節嚴重, 修尚儒學, and 足不逾閾者數年.

proposals.before: He died under Shi rule; cousin Mai continued the line.
proposals.after: In the end he died under the Shi clan; his clansman Zhi's son Mai was appointed heir.
proposals.reason: 族人峙子邁 is Zhi's son Mai, a clansman, not simply cousin Mai.

proposals.before: Pei Xian, style Jingsi,
proposals.after: Xian’s courtesy name was Jingsi.
proposals.reason: The idiomatic field is a sentence fragment.

proposals.before: Yi and Gu inherited literary fame.
proposals.after: Xian had two sons, Yi and Gu, both famed for literary talent.
proposals.reason: The idiomatic line omits that they are Xian’s two sons.

proposals.before: When distinguished figures were few, men mostly traded praise of administrative talent—thinking to glorify house and state—is this not precisely what Chen Qian meant!
proposals.after: When distinguished figures were few, men mostly traded praise of administrative talent—thinking to glorify house and state—is this not a description of Chen Qian!
proposals.reason: 豈陳騫之謂歟 means ‘is this not what is meant by Chen Qian,’ not that Chen Qian ‘meant’ the remark.

decisions.after: The court summoned him as Major to the Minister of State, Chief Clerk, and Palace Assistant Censor, then promoted him to Imperial Secretary and enfeoffed him as Marquis of An'guo Village.
decisions.reason: 遷尚書 names the Shangshu / Imperial Secretary post, not 尚書令 (Director of the Department of State Affairs). The proposed untranslated 'Shangshu' is accurate in rank but not natural idiomatic English.
遷黃門侍郎 is promotion to Gentleman of the Yellow Gate, not 侍中; 侍中 comes last. 厲將校左軍、大司農、侍中 is successive office-holding, not leading a colonel's corps then returning to a palace corps.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 遷黃門侍郎，厲將校左軍、大司農、侍中。

decisions.reason: 遷黃門侍郎 is promotion to Gentleman of the Yellow Gate; 'entered the palace corps' conflates it with 侍中 and omits the actual office.
The literal likewise renders 黃門侍郎 as Palace Attendant (侍中); Gentleman of the Yellow Gate is the correct office.
遷尚書 is the Shangshu post, not 尚書令. Leaving Shangshu in the literal column correctly distinguishes the later Director appointment.
尚書僕射陳泰 is Vice Director of the Imperial Secretariat, not Minister of the Left; 黃門侍郎鍾會 is Gentleman of the Yellow Gate, not Palace Attendant.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 尚書僕射陳泰、黃門侍郎鍾會

decisions.reason: 轉尚書 is transfer to a Shangshu post. 尚書令 appears only later (武帝既即王位，拜尚書令), so Director of the Department of State Affairs overstates the office.
遷尚書僕射 is promotion to Vice Director of the Imperial Secretariat; the Chinese does not specify left 僕射 (Minister of the Left).
加給事中 is a concurrent Given Attendance within the Palace, not 侍中 (Palace Attendant).
The literal repeats the same 給事中 / Palace Attendant confusion; Given Attendance within the Palace matches the Chinese office.
浚庶子憬 is Jun's son by a concubine, separately enfeoffed; 以浚少弟頠嗣 makes Jun's younger brother Yi the main-line heir. 'Legitimate junior uncle' is invented kinship.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 浚庶子憬不惠，別封高陽亭侯，以浚少弟頠嗣

decisions.reason: The sentence is 遇頠，問太傅所在: Liu Yu met Yi and asked for the Grand Tutor. The original omits that meeting and invents the personal name Sima Liang, which the Chinese does not give.
The stray closing quote is not in the Chinese. 西掖門 is the Western Lateral Gate, not a generic western portal.
以儲皇極 means the Eastern Palace exists to hold the heir as the imperial pole (儲 = heir). 'Store up the imperial standard' misreads 儲 as 'store'.
頠 here is the same man named Pei Wei in the following treatise sentence. Rendering him as Yi in this unit splits one person across two English names; the given name is Wei, not Yi.
The literal likewise calls 頠 'Yi' while the next owned unit already uses Pei Wei for the same subject.
梁王肜 is Sima Rong (肜). Sima Yong would be a different prince (typically 顒) and is not in this sentence.
出後從伯凱 is adoption out during life to his father's cousin Kai, not a posthumous adoption and not a simple paternal uncle.
父徽 is Hui. The original 'father Wei' confuses the personal name 徽 with the polity 魏 in 魏冀州刺史.
從兄衍 is Kai's elder cousin Yan. The Chinese does not surname him Wang; 'cousin Wang Yan' invents an identity the source does not state.
眾人為之震恐 is the people present who were terrified. Luoyang is not in the Chinese.
徽比王祥 is Hui, not Wei. 邈比王玄雲 pairs Miao with Wang Xuan; 雲 is the sentence particle, not a second given name Xuanyun.
The original drops 弱冠, 折節嚴重, 修尚儒學, and 足不逾閾者數年. The replacement restores those facts without adding extras.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 及弱冠，更折節嚴重，修尚儒學，足不逾閾者數年

decisions.reason: 族人峙子邁 is the son Mai of clansman Zhi, appointed heir. 'Cousin Mai' collapses two people and misstates the kinship.

憲字景思 is a name-heading that the chapter regularly renders as a fragment. 'Pei Xian, style Jingsi,' already names him and his courtesy name; turning it into a full sentence is stylistic, not a semantic repair.
憲有二子：挹、㲄 states that Yi and Gu are Xian's two sons, both famed for literary talent. The original omits the filiation and the count.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 憲有二子：挹、㲄，並以文才知名

decisions.reason: 豈陳騫之謂歟 is the idiom 'is this not what is meant of Chen Qian' / a description of him, not a claim that Chen Qian 'meant' the preceding remark.

claimRetractions.reason: s0140 names the man only as 太傅. The personal name Sima Liang was supplied by the rejected idiomatic English, not by the Chinese.
Royal-family membership was inferred from the invented personal name Sima Liang. The unit only attests a Grand Tutor (太傅).
The English name 'Yi' for 頠 in s0200 is a mistransliteration. The same person is Pei Wei (Wei); no source-based given name Yi remains once the translation is repaired.
